title: When You Feel Unworthy — Isaiah 6:5
paragraphs: When You Feel Unworthy — Isaiah 6:5
Isaiah didn’t say, “Send me.”
Not first.
He said, “Woe is me… for I am ruined.” (Isaiah 6:5)
That is the part we don’t like to post.

The shaking.
The exposure.
The moment God’s holiness gets so close that every mask falls off and you finally see what you really are without Him.

Unclean.
Undone.
Unworthy.
And maybe that’s where you are right now.

You love God, but you remember what you did.
You want to pray, but shame keeps choking your words.
You want to serve, but the voice in your head keeps whispering, Not you. Not after that. Not with that past.
But here’s what we miss:

Isaiah’s unworthiness did not disqualify him from God’s call.
It positioned him for God’s cleansing.

A coal from the altar touched his lips.
Grace moved first.
God did not argue with Isaiah’s sin.
He answered it with atonement.
“Your guilt is taken away and your sin atoned for.” (Isaiah 6:7)
That is the Gospel.

Jesus is the greater altar.
The greater cleansing.
The greater mercy.

You do not become worthy and then come to Christ.
You come to Christ because you are not worthy — and He is.

So when shame tells you to back away, bow lower.
When guilt tells you the door is closed, look again at the cross.
The blood of Jesus does not cover almost enough.
It covers fully.
Yes, you are aware of your sin.
But if you are in Christ, be more aware of His mercy.

Your unworthiness is real.
But His grace is greater.

So stop treating your failure like it is stronger than the sacrifice of Jesus.
Repent.
Receive.
Rise.

The same God who exposed Isaiah also restored him.
And the same voice that revealed his brokenness was the voice that still called him.

You are not hopeless.
You are not discarded.
You are not too filthy for the fire of God’s grace.

From ruin to redemption.
From shame to sending.
That is what Jesus does.
We tell the stories that shame tried to erase.
